However, E343–362 principally describes subjective experience, and E282–296 offers a conditional argument about divine power; explicit exclusion of relevant evidence remains unestablished."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 415,
      "endEvent": 416,
      "contextStartEvent": 379,
      "contextEndEvent": 580,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "It's something that is huge and is something terrific. And it's false.",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "yes",
      "protection": "no",

      ],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "The concluding verdict treats supernatural religious belief as false after describing its importance. Earlier doctrinal objections address particular Christian teachings; later distinctions between comfort and truth establish insufficient support, not falsity. No general disproof earns this broader verdict. B nevertheless expressly allows that he may be wrong at E576–580."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 941,
      "endEvent": 944,
      "contextStartEvent": 932,
      "contextEndEvent": 969,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "God gave us free will. God gave us free will.",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "yes",
      "protection": "unclear",

        "none"
      ],
      "confidence": "high",
      "explanation": "A answers B's objection to crucifixion as God's method of forgiveness with a repeated affirmation of free will, supplying no connection between human freedom and that method. She then changes subjects at E944–969. Invoking their agreement to disagree limits discussion here, but does not clearly immunize the claim against criticism."
    }
